匿.meaning: When guests arrive, a <part>young</part> puppy leaps into the open sock <part>drawer</part> and pulls a sock over its head. Only its tail pokes out, wagging hard. It is sure it has found the perfect place to <kanji>hide</kanji>.
匿.on: The clock on the dresser goes tick-<sound>tock</sound>, counting how long it lasts.
匿.kun: A <sound>ca</sound>lm old cat curls up beside it like a <sound>cu</sound>shion and shelters it until <sound>Ma</sound>ma leaves.

宰.meaning: From the <part>roof</part> of her restaurant, the head chef watches the kitchen through a skylight, chewing a raw <part>chili</part> to stay sharp. Too much salt? She drops down a note. Burnt rice? Another note. She doesn't cook; she's there to <kanji>superintend</kanji>.
宰.on: Up there she keeps a jug of <sound>ci</sound>der to cool her mouth after the chili.

妄.meaning: A <part>woman</part> buys an old cottage with a mossy, nameless <part>tombstone</part> in the garden and decides it's a doorway to fairyland. Every night she knocks on it, asks for tea, and swears a fairy pours her a cup. Nobody is there: it's a cosy <kanji>delusion</kanji>.
妄.on: Every Sunday she trims round it with a tiny lawn <sound>mow</sound>er, so the fairies won't trip.
妄.kun: '<sound>Me</sound>? Drink your tea without asking?' she scolds a <sound>du</sound>ck that waddles in and helps itself.

腫.meaning: By the light of the <part>moon</part>, a tree doctor climbs an old oak and finds a <part>heavy</part>, knobbly lump bulging from its trunk, round as a football. She taps it: solid wood, no nest, no hive. The oak has grown a <kanji>tumor</kanji>.
腫.on: Squirrels use the lump as a table for the <sound>su</sound>gar cubes they steal from picnics.
腫.kun: She wraps a bandage round it and builds a little <sound>hu</sound>t over it to keep rain off the swelling.

肪.meaning: On a freezing night under the <part>moon</part>, a sailor drifts past a whale sleeping at the surface. Its thick blubber keeps it so warm that frost melts on its back, so he spreads his wet <part>sail</part> across it to dry. Whales are built to be <kanji>obese</kanji>: their fat is their winter coat.
肪.on: When the whale rolls over, its back rises from the sea like a giant <sound>bou</sound>lder.

粧.meaning: Behind a garden <part>shed</part>, a scarecrow wants to look its best for the harvest fair. It powders its face with crushed <part>rice</part> and rubs red <part>soil</part> on its cheeks for blush. The crows have never seen it so pretty: homemade <kanji>cosmetics</kanji>.
粧.on: It wins first prize at the fair's scarecrow beauty <sound>show</sound>.

茂.meaning: A knight leaves his <part>battle axe</part> lying in a meadow for one summer. When he comes back, the <part>grass</part> has swallowed it: only the shiny blade pokes up from a jungle of weeds taller than his horse. The whole field is <kanji>overgrown</kanji>.
茂.on: Even the axe handle has turned furry with green <sound>mo</sound>ss.
茂.kun: '<sound>She</sound> <sound>ge</sound>ts it out first!' shouts his little sister, diving into the weeds.
